title: Marlow Institute
text: The Marlow Institute is a research university founded in 1891 in the city of Varenne. Its first president was Elena Vosk.

title: Elena Vosk
text: Elena Vosk (1850-1923) was a chemist born in Tallis. She served as the first president of the Marlow Institute and later founded the Vosk Prize.

title: Varenne
text: Varenne is a port city on the Selka River with a population of about 410,000. It is home to the Marlow Institute and the Orrin Observatory.

title: Orrin Observatory
text: The Orrin Observatory was completed in 1902 in Varenne. Its main telescope, the Halden Refractor, has a 92 cm lens.

title: Tallis
text: Tallis is a mountain town in the Brenner Highlands, known for copper mining. Its population is about 12,000.

title: Vosk Prize
text: The Vosk Prize is awarded every two years for work in analytical chemistry. It was first awarded in 1925 to Piotr Anand.

title: Piotr Anand
text: Piotr Anand (1889-1961) was a chemist who studied at the Marlow Institute. He received the first Vosk Prize in 1925 for a method of measuring trace metals.

title: Selka River
text: The Selka River is 640 km long. It rises in the Brenner Highlands and flows through Varenne into the Gray Sea.

title: Kessel University
text: Kessel University was founded in 1924 in the city of Dunmore. Its first president was Rafael Ortiz.

title: Dunmore
text: Dunmore is an inland city with a population of about 280,000. It hosts Kessel University.

title: Halden Refractor
text: The Halden Refractor, built by the optician Mira Halden, was the largest lens telescope in the region until 1950.

title: Copper mining in the Brenner Highlands
text: Copper mining in the Brenner Highlands began around 1840. The mines near Tallis closed in 1978 after copper prices fell.

title: 2019 Selka flood
text: In March 2019 the Selka River flooded parts of Varenne. The Orrin Observatory was closed for two months for repairs.

title: Orrin Observatory public program
text: In 2021 the Orrin Observatory restarted its public night program, which had been paused since the 2019 flood.

title: Gray Sea fisheries
text: Fishing in the Gray Sea is regulated by quotas set each year. Cod and herring are the main catches.
